task: WF-6 Refund Cascade Sync Confirmation — adversarial failure-mode probing
attack_surface_explored: Loyalty point double-refund / no-refund on cashBack vs refundPoints sequencing
Mirror order self-cascade through OrderCreated event listeners
OrderPaymentStatusChanged dispatch absence on cashBack — broadcast hole
Cross-branch refund tool authz when controller layer skipped
Idempotency drift across cashBack + RefundWithCounterEntryService double-invocation
Outbox broadcast hole for refund events

findings.title: cashBack() does NOT update parent.payment_status and does NOT dispatch OrderPaymentStatusChanged — refund payment_status sync silently invisible to outbox/realtime listeners
evidence: PaymentService::cashBack lines 90-156 — payment_status never set to PaymentStatus::REFUNDED. The parent order's payment_status remains PaidStatus::PAID after cashBack() returns.
OrderPaymentStatusChanged::dispatch never called from cashBack (grep confirmed: only OrderService:2040 dispatches it).
EventServiceProvider:156 wires OrderPaymentStatusChanged to PersistOrderPaymentStatusChangedToOutbox — the ONLY outbox broadcast path for payment_status changes.

Consequence: connected POS/admin/OSS clients listening on private-branch.{id} do NOT receive a 'refund happened' broadcast. They learn the order is refunded ONLY by re-polling, or by inspecting Transaction.type='cash_back' row, or via ZReport mirror aggregate.
findings.trigger_scenario: Admin issues a cashBack via PaymentService::cashBack (pre-Z path or post-Z mirror path). Order DB row keeps payment_status=PAID (UI semantically wrong) and no realtime broadcast goes out. KDS/POS dashboards do not refresh.
findings.compounding_factor: RefundWithCounterEntryService also never dispatches OrderPaymentStatusChanged — only creates mirror with payment_status=REFUNDED on the MIRROR order, not on the parent. Same broadcast hole.
findings.recommendation: V1.0.1 heal: after cashBack() succeeds, dispatch OrderPaymentStatusChanged($order, OLD=PAID, NEW=REFUNDED) and/or set $order->payment_status = REFUNDED. Alternatively, register a dedicated PersistRefundCreatedToOutbox listener on RefundCreated event.
findings.verdict: P1 GAP — visible to operators as 'refund happened but order still shows PAID until refresh'.

findings.title: Post-Z refund (PosOrderController::refundWithCounterEntry) does NOT refund loyalty points — caller-layer omission

PaymentService::cashBack callers: OrderService.php:1696 — cancel-status path, refundPoints called at line 1702 immediately after.
OrderService.php:1799 — cancel-status path, refundPoints called at line 1805 immediately after.
FrontendOrderService.php:701 — kiosk cancel path, refundPoints called at line 707 immediately after.
caller_layer_audit.verdict_for_cashBack_path: All cashBack() callers PAIR with refundPoints() at the controller/service-orchestrator layer. No loyalty hole for the pre-Z cancel path.
RefundWithCounterEntryService::execute c: PosOrderController.php:64 (refundWithCounterEntry action) — calls $service->execute($order, $reason). Does NOT call LoyaltyService::refundPoints. Only HTTP response handling + branch authz.
caller_layer_audit.verdict_for_counter_entry_path: PosOrderController::refundWithCounterEntry is the SOLE caller of execute(). It does NOT companion-call refundPoints(). This is the real gap.

evidence: LoyaltyService::refundPoints is invoked from 3 sites: OrderService:1702, OrderService:1805, FrontendOrderService:707. All cancel paths.
RefundWithCounterEntryService::execute is invoked from 1 site: PosOrderController::refundWithCounterEntry at line 64. NO refundPoints call alongside.

Consequence: a customer who redeemed loyalty points on an order that is later refunded post-Z via the admin POS refund-with-counter-entry button loses BOTH the cash (refunded via mirror) AND the loyalty points (consumed permanently). Business-invariant violation specifically in the post-Z refund flow.
findings.trigger_scenario: Customer redeems 100 loyalty points worth -€10 on order #1234. Day closes (Z report). Day +1 admin opens order details and clicks 'Refund with Counter-Entry'. PosOrderController::refundWithCounterEntry → RefundWithCounterEntryService::execute. Mirror created with NEGATED total; fiscal chain extends. Customer's 100 points are gone — never reversed because PosOrderController does not call LoyaltyService::refundPoints.
findings.test_evidence_gap: OrderCancellationLoyaltyTest covers cancel path (refundPoints called via OrderService). NO test covers loyalty reversal on RefundWithCounterEntryService::execute or on the PosOrderController::refundWithCounterEntry route.
findings.recommendation: V1.0.1 heal options: (a) add LoyaltyService::refundPoints($order, 'pos') call inside PosOrderController::refundWithCounterEntry right after $service->execute($order, $reason); (b) register a RefundLoyaltyPointsOnRefundCreated listener on RefundCreated event (centralizes loyalty cascade at the event layer for both cashBack and counter-entry paths); (c) move loyalty reversal INSIDE RefundWithCounterEntryService::execute itself (closest to the fiscal transaction).
findings.preferred_heal: Option (b) — listener on RefundCreated event — because it removes the omission risk for future refund entry points and unifies loyalty cascade with stock/availability cascade. Idempotency via LoyaltyTransaction.type='manual_add' lookup against this order_id is straightforward.
findings.verdict: P1 GAP CONFIRMED — caller-layer audit confirms post-Z refund path skips loyalty reversal. Pre-Z cancel path is safe (3 callers all pair). Fiscal cascade COMPLETE; loyalty cascade INCOMPLETE on post-Z path only.

findings.title: Mirror order does NOT self-cascade — Order::create() inside RefundWithCounterEntryService is safe
evidence: AppServiceProvider:67 attaches SoftDeleteAuditObserver to Order — this observer writes audit rows on soft-delete, NOT dispatches OrderCreated.

OrderCreated::dispatch is called explicitly at OrderService:564, 1067, 1377 and FrontendOrderService:1226 — all explicit dispatch sites, none triggered by Order::create() in RefundWithCounterEntryService:95.
Mirror order with negated quantity therefore does NOT trigger DecrementStockOnOrderCreated → would have caused double-release if it had.

findings.title: RefundCreated listener exception in sync mode silently kills downstream listeners
evidence: QUEUE_CONNECTION=sync (default test + production-Le-Cayenne). EventServiceProvider:165-168 lists ReleaseStockOnRefundCreated BEFORE ReleaseAvailabilityOnRefundCreated.

If ReleaseStockOnRefundCreated throws (StockService::releaseForOrder failure — e.g., missing StockLevel row, integrity error), the exception propagates up the Laravel event dispatcher and ReleaseAvailabilityOnRefundCreated NEVER fires.

Parent order is committed, audit chain extended, mirror created (in RefundWithCounterEntryService path) — but availability counters stay decremented forever. Items remain 'sold out' until manual heal.

Same vulnerability documented in EventServiceProvider:128-137 for OrderStatusChanged. The fix doctrine there was: Outbox-first listener + try/catch wrap inside FCM listener. Refund cascade has NEITHER protection (no outbox listener AND no try/catch in stock/availability listeners).
findings.trigger_scenario: Branch has a StockLevel row deletion (operator error in catalog UI). Subsequent refund of an order containing that item throws inside ReleaseStockOnRefundCreated → ReleaseAvailabilityOnRefundCreated skipped → availability counter never released → item shows 0 stock permanently in UI.
findings.recommendation: V1.0.1 heal: wrap ReleaseStockOnRefundCreated body in try/catch + Log::warning (defense in depth) OR reorder listeners (availability release first, stock release second, since availability is the user-visible counter).
findings.verdict: P2 GAP — degraded resilience but bounded blast radius.

findings.title: Customer deletion does NOT block refund — orphaned audit and orphaned mirror are possible
evidence: RefundWithCounterEntryService:95-112 sets mirror's user_id = $parent->user_id without verifying customer still exists.
If parent.user_id was soft-deleted between sale and refund, mirror Order references a deleted user. Eloquent withTrashed() relations work but UI joins assume active users.

LoyaltyService::refundPoints (the cancellation path) DOES handle this via line 47-54 — logs warning + returns. But the refund cascade itself never queries User for the mirror; orphaned mirror persists silently.
findings.recommendation: V1.0.2 — add User::withTrashed() guard in mirror creation path and surface a warning audit row if customer was deleted. Non-blocking for V1.

findings.title: Idempotency on cashBack() prevents double-RefundCreated dispatch — proven by test
evidence: PaymentService::cashBack:92-98 early-returns if existing Transaction.type='cash_back' is found.
RefundCreated dispatch happens INSIDE 'if ($transaction)' block (line 145), so second cashBack() call hits the early-return BEFORE reaching dispatch.
RefundCreatedDispatchTest::test_cashback_idempotent_call_does_not_re_dispatch_event explicitly asserts only 1 dispatch across 2 cashBack() calls. PASSING.

findings.title: Idempotency on RefundWithCounterEntryService::execute prevents double-mirror
evidence: Line 73-78 refuses if parent.status === RETURNED. After first successful execute(), parent's status would be... wait — actually parent.status is NEVER changed by execute(). The guard relies on the MIRROR existing with parent_order_id=parent.id?

Looking deeper: line 73 checks parent.status (not mirror count). But parent.status is set ONLY by the calling controller (which transitions parent to RETURNED before/after calling this service). If a future caller invokes execute() twice without transitioning parent → DOUBLE MIRROR. Mitigation depends on caller discipline.
Sentinel test RefundCounterEntryRequiresSealedParentSentinelTest covers the sealed-parent guard but not the 'parent.status set externally' invariant.
findings.verdict: ACCEPTABLE per current caller pattern — but flag as a 'be careful when refactoring caller' risk; recommend adding an explicit 'mirror already exists' check (SELECT mirror WHERE parent_order_id = parent.id LIMIT 1) for defense in depth in V1.0.2.

findings.title: RefundCreated::dispatch($parent) passes PARENT, not mirror — critical correctness
evidence: RefundWithCounterEntryService:229 — RefundCreated::dispatch($parent). Comment block lines 224-229 explicitly explains why: 'mirror has NEGATED qty which would no-op / corrupt the released_qty ledger'.

ReleaseAvailabilityOnRefundCreated:30-44 iterates $event->order->orderItems and uses (int)$orderItem->quantity as POSITIVE release amount. If mirror were passed, qty=-N would feed into AvailabilityService.releaseForOrderItems with negative qty → silent no-op or undefined behavior.
ReleaseStockOnRefundCreated:12 delegates to StockService::releaseForOrder which iterates parent.orderItems().get() — same positivity assumption.
findings.verdict: CONFIRMED — design choice documented and correct.

coverage_gap_observed: No test asserting OrderPaymentStatusChanged fires on cashBack — would catch R-1.
No test asserting LoyaltyService::refundPoints fires via RefundCreated cascade — would catch R-2.
No test asserting RefundWithCounterEntryService refunds loyalty points — would catch R-2.
No test asserting availability release survives stock-release exception — would catch R-4.

verdict: REFUND CASCADE FISCAL SAFE but BUSINESS CASCADE INCOMPLETE. 2 P1 findings (R-1 payment_status broadcast hole + R-2 loyalty no-reversal), 2 P2 (R-4 cross-listener exception, R-5 deleted customer), 3 INFO (R-3 mirror safety, R-6/R-7 idempotency, R-8 dispatch correctness). V1 Le Cayenne acceptable; V1.0.1 heal mandatory before SaaS expansion (loyalty business rule violation is a customer-trust issue).
